name: Hattush
overview: Hattush was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as an Aaronic priest. He is specifically mentioned in the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role in the religious leadership of Israel during that period. His priestly office underscores his dedication to the service of God as part of the Levitical priesthood.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hattush' appears only once in Scripture and carries no recorded meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional significance provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hattush as a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, which situates him within the priestly lineage essential for temple service. Beyond this inferred relationship, no other family connections are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Hattush's inclusion among the signatories of the Nehemiah covenant document signifies his commitment to uphold the renewed covenant with God. As an Aaronic priest, his role was vital in maintaining the spiritual and ceremonial purity of Israel during the post-exilic restoration. His presence in Nehemiah 10:4 marks him as a faithful leader supporting the community's return to obedience under God's law.
